newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland govt faces no-confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland govt faces no-confidence motion.

text.p: The Queensland state government will face a no-confidence motion later on Thursday from the Labor opposition after premier Rob Borbidge refused to call back an government-appointed inquiry into pre-election deals.
Labor's move could see an end to the eight-month administration of the Borbidge government which relies on the support of one independent member.
However, Independent Liz Cunningham who holds the balance of power in State Parliament, indicated on Wednesday that she was unlikely to support the Labor motion.

Former New South Wales judge Kenneth Carruthers resigned from heading the incomplete inquiry on Tuesday after citing interference from a separate government-appointed inquiry into the state's Criminal Justice Commission.

Opposition leader Peter Beattie advised Borbidge by letter that Labor MPs would move the no-confiidence motion unless the terms of reference of the government inquiry were amended so that it would not interfere with Carruthers' investigations.
"Were this action to be taken, I would hope that Mr Carruthers would then agree to complete this report since his independence would by that action be reinstated," Beattie said in the letter.

Beattie said on Wednesday the no-confidence motion would be moved after Borbidge had indicated there would be no proposal to change the terms of reference of the government's inquiry into the Criminal Justice Commission.
